# Nexus Consulting Services Limited

> A Zambian IT consultancy in Lusaka that builds, configures and operates the
> infrastructure regulated businesses need to demonstrate compliance to a
> regulator, auditor or board - not just have it work.

Nexus has traded since 2017 and incorporated as a limited company in 2020
(PACRA 120200003611). It is a small, hands-on team - the managing consultant
delivers the work directly rather than routing it through account managers.
Most clients are Zambian businesses that answer to someone: a banking or
microfinance regulator, an auditor, a board, or a customer asking where its
data is kept.

## Services

- Cyber security & compliance: security awareness and phishing-simulation
  programmes, gap assessments, policy packs, incident-response plans, and the
  documentation an examiner expects.
- Microsoft 365 & infrastructure: tenant hardening, MFA and Conditional
  Access, Microsoft Defender, mail-flow and email authentication, firewall
  hardening, site-to-site VPN, and 3CX telephony.
- Web design & development: business websites built to load quickly on a
  Zambian mobile connection, structured to be found in search, handed over
  with full credentials and documentation.
- Hosting & domains: managed hosting on infrastructure Nexus operates,
  domain registration and renewal, business email, SSL, backups and
  monitoring, billed as an annual retainer.
- Business systems: custom software where an off-the-shelf product doesn't
  fit - a loan management system and a credit-risk dashboard are both live
  in production today.
- ICT supply & procurement: hardware, licensing and network equipment
  sourced and configured, ready to use rather than ready to unbox.

## The security-awareness programme

Nexus's flagship offering. Every regulated lender in Zambia carries some
version of the same audit finding: staff security awareness is not being
measured. The platforms built to close it are priced per seat in US dollars,
which is not viable for a sixty-person microfinance institution. Nexus's
managing consultant built an affordable, open-source-based alternative and
ran it inside a Bank of Zambia-supervised institution, where it closed the
finding it was commissioned for. Nexus now deploys and operates that
programme for clients: monthly phishing simulation, automatic remedial
training for anyone who fails a simulation, new-joiner security onboarding,
and quarterly content refresh - all with no per-seat fee and no forex
exposure. Full detail: https://mynexusgroup.com/services/security-awareness/

## How engagements work

1. A short, free scoping call establishes what needs fixing, by when, and
   for whom.
2. Before any commitment, the client gets something concrete and free: a
   findings sheet on their current exposure, or a working site mock-up.
3. Scope and price are agreed in writing before work starts. Nexus does not
   bill by the hour.
4. Delivery includes documentation, credentials and administrative access -
   clients are never locked in by Nexus holding a password.
5. An ongoing retainer, if one is needed, is a separate decision taken after
   delivery.

## Selected work

- NdalamaHub - a full loan management platform for a collateral-backed
  lender: borrower intake, application review queue, disbursement controls,
  a rollover engine, a collateral register, and a portfolio/NPL dashboard.
  Live in production. https://mynexusgroup.com/work/ndalamahub/
- ManifiPay - public website for a Lusaka lender, wired directly into their
  loan system so an online enquiry becomes a reviewable application without
  re-typing. https://mynexusgroup.com/work/manifipay/
- A security-awareness programme run inside a Bank of Zambia-supervised
  institution (unnamed - the institution's control environment is sensitive;
  named on request with client consent).
- Around ten organisations across food production, professional services
  and consulting are hosted and maintained on annual retainers, several
  since 2019.

## Who Nexus serves

Microfinance and lending institutions, professional services firms, food
production and retail businesses, and NGOs and associations - concentrated
in Zambia, with the compliance-driven work concentrated in Bank of
Zambia-supervised lenders.
